public_rationale: The ordinary current-system reading holds. A leading reasoning-capable model still failed benchmark tasks, and independent repeated-run research found that reasoning prompts did not provide uniform consistency. Narrow successes, including a reported zero-error editing benchmark, do not establish correct performance across tasks every time. The evidence does not support extending this verdict to all future systems.
limitations: One source is a vendor evaluation and the independent study is a preprint.
The independent study tests reasoning prompts rather than every dedicated reasoning-model architecture.
The model announcement and the post share a publication date; their intraday order is not established.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Regardless of added reasoning, LLMs cannot be trusted to do things correctly or consistently every time.

statement.excerpt: You can add as many levels of intrigue and “reasoning” as you want, but Large Language Models cannot be trusted to do something correctly, or even consistently, every time.

our_interpretation: The plain reading is that existing LLMs, including reasoning-enhanced systems, do not guarantee correct, repeatable performance across user tasks.
This does not mean every task fails, every repeated answer differs, or no bounded application can be reliable.
For this ongoing technical observation, use the latest quarter-to-date before publication: July 1 through September 29, 2025. Model evaluations have no uniform financial-style reporting cycle.
The observation concerns available reasoning methods, not a proof about every possible future architecture.
criteria.support_condition: Evaluations in the target period show nonzero task failures in reasoning-capable systems and variation across repeated runs despite reasoning prompts or other enhancements.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Evidence establishes general correct and repeatable performance across the relevant tasks with added reasoning; a perfect score on one finite, narrow benchmark is insufficient.
